evidence: kerberos-realms-against-the-dc: manifest 40-47 writes /etc/krb5.conf from krb5.conf.erb, whose line 6 sets default_realm from domain_netbios_name.domain_tld; the probe reads default_realm and runs kinit with and without the realm against the DC. The upper-case expectation (P8TEST.EXAMPLE) is what the current template produces under local change #17 (rules/local_changes.md row 17, upcase on line 6), and it is that row's after-check; the baseline line alone would render P8TEST.example, which is the row's before evidence. Probe+expect test the purpose (a realm-less kinit works) of the cited lines

pam-logins-through-winbind: manifest 31-38 writes pam_winbind.conf from the template whose line 30 sets require_membership_of to the prefixed groups (P8TEST+p8testgroup); smb.conf.erb:19 sets winbind use default domain = yes; openvpn_server.pp:169 pam => true (plugin via login). pamtester login auth+acct: member accepted with prefix and bare name, wrong password refused, outsider refused while wbinfo -a shows the DC accepts its password, isolating the membership rule. Matches the lines under the params fixture

the-node-is-joined-to-the-domain: manifest 86-88 runs join-domain.sh (net join -U join_user) unless the join user resolves; net rpc testjoin printing Join to 'P8TEST' is OK tests the machine account the join creates. Mismatch varies the workgroup to a nonexistent domain P8NOPE, a value whose change must change the verdict, and changes only that value

purpose covered: Purpose (join an OpenVPN node to AD so listed-group domain users log in with their domain password) matches the baseline manifest and templates. Tested: smb.conf as domain member, machine account working on the node and held by the DC, domain users/groups resolving through nsswitch+winbind (with a mismatch user), pam_winbind require_membership_of and /etc/pam.d/openvpn byte-identical, real PAM logins through login (member ok with prefix and bare name; wrong password and outsider refused; DC accepts outsider so refusal is the membership rule), Kerberos realm-less and realm kinit against the DC, WINS host resolution via nsswitch's wins source to the DNS address (with an unknown-name mismatch). Not separately probed: the package list (ntpdate, cifs-utils) and the /etc/pam.d directory attributes, which are prerequisites rather than purpose outcomes; /etc/pam.d/openvpn is used by no baseline service (openvpn_server's PAM plugin uses login), so it is honestly checked as installed only.
